disclosure: Fictional teaching cases. No operational records, measured estate results or real approvals.

cases.title: Two titles, one purpose
cases.purpose: Give operations one agreed view of completed transport work.
cases.definition: A completed transport leg, counted once by leg identifier.
cases.population: Fictional contracted rides, completed legs only
cases.cutoff: Both views use the same fictional overnight close
cases.usage: Both views have documented daily consumers; consumer interviews confirm the same use
cases.dependencies: Dispatch review and the daily operations briefing
cases.missing: Replacement acceptance and retirement authorization are still required
cases.action: Validate the replacement with both consumer groups, then request controlled withdrawal of the redundant view.
cases.rollback: Restore the old route if a required field or consumer dependency is missing
cases.intake: Reuse the selected view instead of creating another daily completion report.

evidence.title: Definition comparison
evidence.text: The two views share leg identifier, completed status rule, service-day population and overnight close. No material definition difference was found in this fictional comparison.

evidence.title: Consumer dependency check
evidence.text: The dispatch reviewer and briefing owner confirm the same purpose. Both require replacement acceptance before the redundant route is withdrawn.

evidence.title: Authority decision
evidence.text: The operations reporting owner selects Daily Ride Completion as the proposed source of record because its ownership and maintenance route are explicit. This is a worked recommendation, not a real approval.

stages.title: Establish equivalence
stages.check: Compare definition, population, grain, cutoff, freshness and audience, not the titles.
stages.supported: Equivalent for the stated daily purpose → propose consolidation.
stages.exception: Material difference or missing comparison → retain both provisionally and reconcile the gap.
stages.exit: A documented comparison is ready for the reporting owner.

stages.title: Choose the authoritative view
stages.check: Confirm accountable stewardship and validate all consumer dependencies.
stages.supported: Owner and consumers agree → nominate Daily Ride Completion.
stages.exception: Disputed purpose or ownership → escalate to the reporting lead; no authoritative label yet.
stages.exit: A proposed authority and its rationale are recorded.

stages.title: Transition before withdrawal
stages.check: Reconcile the replacement, communicate the route change and agree rollback and observation conditions.
stages.supported: Acceptance and authorization recorded → begin reversible withdrawal, then monitor before final disposition.
stages.exception: Missing fields or a new dependency → stop withdrawal or restore the old route and return to validation.
stages.exit: Consolidation is proposed; retirement remains gated on recorded acceptance.

cases.title: Same total, different meaning
cases.purpose: Distinguish service performance from financial posting activity.
cases.definition: Service completion and financial posting are different events; a shared headline total does not make them interchangeable.
cases.population: Completed service legs versus posted financial events
cases.audience: Operations and finance consumers with different decisions
cases.classification: Restricted metadata and operational context; no member rows shown
cases.usage: Both owners identify a distinct recurring use
cases.lifecycle: Retain both, distinguish purpose and definition
cases.missing: Shared definition for a proposed combined leadership metric is unresolved
cases.action: Label both event clocks and keep the combined metric on hold until its definition is agreed.
cases.rollback: Not applicable: neither existing view is withdrawn
cases.intake: A combined view requires a new agreed metric contract, not a renamed existing report.

evidence.title: Event-grain comparison
evidence.text: Service Day Activity groups completed legs by service date. Posted Activity groups financial events by posting date. Late postings can appear on a different day and several postings can relate to one leg.

evidence.title: Owner disagreement
evidence.text: Operations needs service performance; finance needs posted activity. Neither owner has approved a common interpretation of the proposed leadership headline. The disagreement remains explicit.

stages.title: Test the apparent match
stages.check: Trace grain, event time and population behind the matching headline.
stages.supported: Different business meaning → document a legitimate variant.
stages.exception: If the definitions are actually equivalent → return to the authority and dependency review before consolidating.

stages.title: Protect each intended use
stages.check: Name the decision each view supports and label its time basis.
stages.supported: Distinct purposes confirmed → retain both with clear names and ownership.
stages.exception: An owner cannot explain a distinct use → investigate; do not infer retirement from a matching total.
stages.exit: Both views remain, with their purpose and limits documented.

stages.title: Hold the disputed combined claim
stages.check: Obtain an agreed definition before publishing a combined leadership metric.
stages.supported: Definition agreed later → validate the combined use against its own requirements.
stages.exception: Definition still disputed → keep that combined request on hold and assign the metric steward to reconcile it.
stages.exit: Existing uses continue; the unsupported combined claim does not proceed.

cases.title: Quiet but essential
cases.purpose: Support a periodic contract review that daily usage logs can miss.
cases.definition: Open contract exceptions at the agreed reporting close
cases.cutoff: Agreed review period, not a daily reporting window
cases.channel: Existing restricted workspace; no new delivery authorized
cases.usage: Recent daily log has incomplete coverage and does not span a contract-review cycle
cases.missing: Complete cadence-appropriate use evidence and field-level classification
cases.action: Confirm the next review dependency with the owner and collect evidence across its actual cadence.
cases.rollback: Not applicable: withdrawal is not authorized
cases.intake: Record periodic use and the next review trigger so a quiet asset is not mistaken for an abandoned one.

evidence.title: Incomplete usage window
evidence.text: The available daily activity log does not cover the contract-review close and excludes the scheduled delivery route. No-use has not been established.

evidence.title: Contract review dependency
evidence.text: The contract reporting owner identifies Period Close Exceptions as an input to the review pack. Its next scheduled use must be protected.

stages.title: Question the quiet log
stages.check: Check the window, telemetry coverage, delivery routes and expected use cadence.
stages.supported: Complete window and all routes covered → assess inactivity with the owner.
stages.exception: Window or coverage incomplete → record unknown use; do not label the asset unused.
stages.exit: Evidence coverage is explicit, including the missing scheduled route.

stages.title: Find the dependency
stages.check: Confirm periodic obligations and downstream pack dependencies.
stages.supported: A required review dependency exists → retain the report for that use.
stages.exception: No dependency established → continue investigation; silence is not approval.
stages.exit: Retirement is held; the next review use is protected.

stages.title: Assign the missing checks
stages.check: Set a cadence-appropriate review and obtain sensitivity classification before any new delivery.
stages.supported: Evidence collected later → return to inventory and retirement assessment.
stages.exception: Classification or coverage remains unknown → maintain restrictions and escalate unresolved ownership to the reporting lead.
stages.exit: A named evidence task replaces an unsupported retirement decision.

cases.title: A replacement, then a late dependency
cases.purpose: Replace a legacy route without disrupting a periodic consumer.
cases.cadence: Daily review plus a periodic export dependency
cases.cutoff: Daily service close; periodic mapping must also be checked
cases.usage: Initial consumer review missed the periodic reconciliation route
cases.dependencies: Daily exception review and a late-discovered reconciliation mapping
cases.lifecycle: Reversible withdrawal stopped; old route restored
cases.missing: Replacement mapping for the periodic consumer and renewed acceptance
cases.action: Restore the old route, retain the candidate, repair its mapping and repeat dependency validation before requesting new approval.
cases.rollback: A required consumer loses a field or dependency during observation
cases.intake: Include periodic and downstream delivery routes in replacement acceptance.

evidence.title: Initial transition record
evidence.text: The fictional owner accepted the daily replacement subject to reversible withdrawal, consumer notice and observation across the required operating cadence. Destruction was not approved.

evidence.title: Late dependency finding
evidence.text: During observation, the periodic reconciliation owner identifies a legacy route key missing from the replacement. The stated rollback condition is met.

evidence.title: Recovery disposition
evidence.text: The worked disposition restores the legacy route, preserves both revisions and returns the replacement to validation. Final retirement and irreversible deletion remain unauthorized.

stages.title: Start a reversible transition
stages.check: Confirm owner approval, consumer notice, replacement acceptance, observation coverage and a recovery route.
stages.supported: All conditions recorded → withdraw reversibly and observe; do not delete.
stages.exception: Any condition missing → hold withdrawal and return to validation.
stages.exit: Only a bounded, recoverable change is allowed in the fictional transition.

stages.title: Evaluate the late finding
stages.check: Determine whether the missing route key breaks a required consumer.
stages.supported: A required dependency is affected → invoke rollback.
stages.exception: No required use is affected → record the reason and continue agreed observation; do not ignore the finding.
stages.exit: The dependency finding changes the disposition.

stages.title: Restore, repair and repeat validation
stages.check: Restore the old route, preserve candidate history and assign replacement mapping repair.
stages.supported: Repair and renewed consumer acceptance recorded later → request a new bounded transition approval.
stages.exception: Repair not yet validated → keep the restored route available and the retirement on hold.
stages.exit: Current disposition: restore and revalidate, not retired.

cases.title: Useful work without sensitive rows
cases.purpose: Let a restricted contributor improve the field dictionary without receiving member-level rows.
cases.definition: Map field meanings using invented values and structural metadata only
cases.population: Synthetic examples, separate from the restricted operational report
cases.cutoff: Not applicable: synthetic metadata has no service-period population
cases.usage: A dictionary review request, not permission to inspect Claim Detail
cases.rollback: Withdraw the alternative if source rows or unreviewed sensitive fields are discovered
cases.intake: Specify the task and permitted fields before selecting a delivery route.

condition.label: Alternative's review evidence
condition.context: Whether the alternative's classification and approval are established decides delivery; switch the condition below to compare both branches.
condition.restriction: No member-row access to Claim Detail is approved in either branch.

branches.classification: Source restricted; alternative explicitly reviewed as synthetic and metadata-only
branches.lifecycle: Alternative permitted within the fictional stated scope
branches.explanation: The fictional reviewer has confirmed the alternative, audience, purpose, fields and channel. Claim Detail remains restricted. Only the Synthetic Field Map is permitted in the stated fictional scope.
branches.action: Provide only the reviewed Synthetic Field Map through the approved metadata workspace.

branches.classification: Unknown: alternative classification and approval not established
branches.explanation: Classification and approval of the alternative are not established. The access reviewer must supply the missing evidence before delivery. Claim Detail remains restricted; the report title or removal of names cannot establish safety.
branches.action: Request authorized review before providing the alternative. Restricted source access remains prohibited.

evidence.title: Task and restriction
evidence.text: The contributor needs names, definitions and invented examples to improve the dictionary. The contributor is not authorized to inspect member-level Claim Detail.

evidence.title: Alternative review
evidence.text: In the known-evidence branch, the authorized access reviewer confirms the Synthetic Field Map contains invented examples and structural metadata only, for the named contributor and purpose, through the approved metadata workspace.

evidence.title: Unknown evidence condition
evidence.text: In the unknown-evidence branch, classification and approval of the alternative have not been established. A synthetic-looking title, redaction or removal of names does not establish safety. Delivery is held pending review.

stages.title: Separate the task from the source
stages.check: Identify the fields and examples needed for dictionary work, then preserve the source restriction.
stages.supported: Task can use invented values and structural metadata → propose a separate alternative.
stages.exception: Task genuinely needs restricted rows → route an access request; do not copy source data into the alternative.
stages.exit: Claim Detail remains restricted in either branch.

stages.title: Check evidence before delivery
stages.check: Confirm classification, purpose, audience, fields, channel and explicit approval for the alternative.
stages.supported: Known reviewed alternative → permit only the synthetic field map for that stated use.
stages.exception: Unknown classification or approval → hold delivery, identify missing evidence and request review.
stages.exit: The evidence condition determines whether the alternative may proceed.

stages.title: Keep the permission bounded
stages.check: Keep the restricted source out of the task and revisit approval if fields, audience, purpose or channel change.
stages.supported: Scope unchanged and evidence known → dictionary work can proceed on the alternative.
stages.exception: Scope changes or sensitive content appears → stop delivery and return to access review.
stages.exit: A fictional access decision is explained; this page grants no actual access.

cases.title: A strategic request at the front door
cases.decision: Hold the disputed metric, progress the ready work
cases.approver: Strategic reporting sponsor and metric owner
cases.purpose: Answer which vendors need attention without inventing an agreed contract-performance definition.
cases.definition: The requested missed-service definition is disputed; the existing operational review does not settle it
cases.population: Fictional contracted vendor services; exclusions await agreement
cases.grain: A proposed vendor-period measure, not yet accepted
cases.cutoff: Period and exclusions must be agreed in the metric contract
cases.classification: Proposed summary requires an approved audience and minimized fields before release
cases.channel: Proposed internal leadership workspace; output not yet approved
cases.usage: A new strategic request has been recorded
cases.dependencies: Metric definition, source lineage, quality evidence and sponsor acceptance
cases.lifecycle: Requested metric held; ready non-dependent work may proceed
cases.missing: Agreed missed-service definition, exclusions and validation evidence
cases.action: Assign the metric steward to reconcile the definition; reuse suitable existing context while holding the unsupported performance claim.
cases.rollback: Return the proposed scorecard to validation if its source, definition or access scope changes
cases.intake: Search existing assets, record reuse gaps and establish definition, owner, access, acceptance and review triggers before new reporting is approved.

evidence.title: Reuse assessment
evidence.text: Vendor Service Review supplies operational context, but its service-status rules do not establish the requested contract-performance measure. Reuse is appropriate for context, not proof of the new claim.

evidence.title: Definition gap
evidence.text: The fictional sponsor and metric owner have not agreed missed-service exclusions or the reporting cutoff. The performance metric lacks an accepted definition and validation evidence.

evidence.title: Bounded readiness decision
evidence.text: The metric steward owns reconciliation. Existing supported operational review and unrelated cleanup can continue. Readiness is assessed for this specific strategic question, not by requiring every legacy report to be retired.

stages.title: Translate the request into a decision
stages.check: State the business question, intended action, audience, cadence and existing reuse candidates.
stages.supported: Existing context fits part of the need → reuse it and identify the remaining gap.
stages.exception: No suitable view exists → justify a new asset through the same controlled intake, not a chat-only build request.
stages.exit: The request and reuse rationale have an accountable sponsor.

stages.title: Check the prerequisites for the claim
stages.check: Confirm definition, population, exclusions, time basis, lineage, quality and permitted audience.
stages.supported: All prerequisites accepted → validate the bounded scorecard use.
stages.exception: Definition still disputed → hold the dependent metric and assign reconciliation.
stages.exit: Unsupported performance claims do not reach leadership.

stages.title: Keep progress bounded and maintainable
stages.check: Separate ready work from blocked work and assign ownership, acceptance and lifecycle review for any new asset.
stages.supported: Independent work is ready → continue it without pretending the disputed metric is resolved.
stages.exception: A task depends on the unresolved metric → keep it held until the definition and evidence are accepted.
stages.exit: A specific readiness gate replaces both uncontrolled building and an estate-wide cleanup freeze.
